provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
In the canonical task, the output is five copies of the input tile concatenated horizontally: original, left-right mirror, original, mirror, original.

The factory conjugates this mechanism by the D4 transform:
- With an odd number of clockwise quarter turns (d4 % 4 in {1, 3}), the strip runs vertically. The copies are stacked top to bottom, and the alternate copies are flipped up-down.
- Otherwise (identity, 180-degree turn, and reflections composed with those), the strip stays horizontal and the alternate copies are flipped left-right.

The tile order O,M,O,M,O is a palindrome, so reversed traversal still puts the unmodified visible tile first. The mirror is conjugated to the appropriate reflection of the visible tile, so mirror(g) remains correct.

The mechanism copies cells and never reads colour values, so the palette needs no specialisation. The emitted program works directly in visible coordinates and handles any tile height and width. The constructor uses 4x4 tiles, giving 4x20 or 20x4 outputs.
draft_notes.limitations: The axis is fixed by d4 at build time and is not inferred from the demonstrations. The constructor only produces 4x4 tiles, but the emitted code generalises to any rectangular tile. No constructor defects or fixture contradictions were found: all approved fixtures match the alternating mirror-tiling rule. The archived solver's background-colour canvas fill is cosmetic, since every cell gets overwritten, so it is omitted. This factory has not been run or tested; the host's verification on the fixtures and fresh pairs is still pending.

independent_source_review.mechanism: The output is five copies of the input tile laid side by side in the order original, left-right mirror, original, mirror, original. The constructor writes output[r][c], output[r][7-c], output[r][8+c], output[r][15-c] and output[r][16+c] into a 4x20 canvas built by common.grid(20, 4) (width 20, height 4). The factory conjugates this by D4. For d4 % 4 odd, it stacks the tiles vertically and uses g[::-1, :] (an up-down flip) as the mirror. Otherwise it concatenates horizontally and uses g[:, ::-1] as the mirror.
evidence: Constructor indices 0..3 and 8..11 and 16..19 hold the original tile, and 7-c and 15-c hold the mirrored tile. This is exactly O,M,O,M,O with no seams or offsets.
All four train fixtures and the test fixture match this construction. For example, test row 0 is 5544|4455|5544|4455|5544.
The labels depend only on the cells of the visible input. The random latents (num_colors and the palette) only shape the input and never select the rule, so no hidden latent determines the output.

D4 conjugation is sound. A quarter turn maps the horizontal strip to a vertical one and maps fliplr to flipud. A reflection or 180-degree turn keeps the axis and leaves the conjugated mirror equal to fliplr. Because the O,M,O,M,O order is a palindrome, a reversed traversal still puts the visible original tile at index 0.
The emitted solver works directly on the visible grid. It slices g and assigns into out, with no untransform/solve/retransform wrapper.
The solver reads no colours, so the palette needs no specialisation. np.zeros is safe because every cell of out is overwritten.
Host audit passed: 1000 fresh pairs, 8000 augmented checks, 16 fixture variants, no sampler rejections.
nonblocking_limits: The tiling axis is fixed at build time from d4 rather than inferred from the demonstrations. This is acceptable because it is a deterministic spatial orientation constant that every demonstration teaches.
The constructor only produces 4x4 tiles, so the solver's generalisation to non-square tiles is not exercised. That case is out of domain.

Correctness assumes the host D4 encoding has odd (d4 % 4) values meaning an odd number of quarter turns, possibly composed with a reflection. The audit passed at d4=7, which is consistent with this, but the encoding table was not supplied.
required_context_checks: Confirm that the host's D4 index convention maps d4 % 4 in {1, 3} to axis-swapping transforms for both the rotation and reflection halves (d4 0-3 and 4-7). It should also confirm that the augmented checks covered at least one even and one odd build value, not only d4=7.
